rows: README: link the hazeljs npm package. A short README section pointing to the experimental hazeljs package, saying it is a 0.0.x prototype that does not track dev yet.
merges cleanly; CI green at its head, 11-06

Modulo by zero: an error, not a crash. int_mod(7, 0), and the SInt, Nat and Float modulos, crashed the interpreter: they named a builtin, mod, that does not exist. Now each gives Divide by Zero, as 7 / 0 does.
merges cleanly; CI green at its head, 11-15
A frame-rate HUD, with ?hud. Frames a second and frame times, in a corner, only when the address has ?hud. One file, index.html.
merges cleanly; CI green at its head, 11-08

Ids minted and compared as strings. An id is built by joining one-byte strings and compared as a string, not through Uuidm's buffer: evaluation about 13% faster on the heaviest programs (the PR's own measurement). On the livelits branch since 2026-10-10.
merges cleanly; CI green at its head, 11-07

The eval worker in Firefox, started at load. Firefox showed Evaluation timed out for answers the worker could give at once, when the page's thread was busy: the worker now starts at load, and a reply waiting in the queue is not timed out. Finding 8 on #2609.
merges cleanly; CI green at its head, 10-05

MapPiece keeps unchanged pieces. A projector update away from the caret copied the whole program; now every piece with nothing changed under it stays the same object. 3.12 to 1.92 ms an update on a 2,000-let program (its benchmark).
merges cleanly; CI green at its head, 10-10

Incremental evaluation around a recursive let. Fixes the free variables statics reports for a recursive let, so an expression with one inside (a module with a recursive member, a function with a recursive helper) is reused, not run again.
merges cleanly; CI green at its head, 10-12
An approval. Alexander noted on 10-29 that #2431 (Matt Keenan's property tests, open) changes this code too: review them side by side.
A module binding analyzes its definition once. Statics analyzed a module's definition twice, once as a let and once directly; now it reads back the elaboration the let recorded. Finding 7 on #2609.
merges cleanly; CI green at its head, 10-21
An approval. Alexander's review of 10-21 is answered, in three commits that day. #2717, below, is an optional follow-up.
Goto first use, Goto next use. Two moves in the context menu, the reverse of Goto definition: to a definition's first use, and from each use to the next. With tests.
merges cleanly; CI green at its head, 11-06

Statics: a let analyzed once unless it refers to itself. Four statics and completion speedups, found by profiling the livelits branch, each its own commit with tests. The big one: a let-bound function no longer takes the recursive path's four passes, which multiplied with nesting. Byte-identical hazel analyze -W output on dev's 72 programs when it was made.
merges cleanly; CI green at its head, 09-26
An approval. Its CI ran on 09-26, 462 commits of dev ago; the merge queue runs it again on today's dev.

Test: the nodes an evaluation builds, held to budgets. Counts the terms an evaluation builds, beside its steps, so copies like those #2679 removed cannot come back unseen. A draft only because it waited on #2678 and #2679, both merged (10-29, 10-19); its own commit is 118 lines added and 29 removed, in 2 files.
merges cleanly; CI green at its head, 10-16
Merge dev in, so its diff is its own commit, and mark it ready.

Colors: every var() is one the theme defines. Eleven var() names that nothing defined, so those colors ignored the Colors slide, dark mode and high contrast; each now reads a theme role, and a lint keeps it so. Approved by Alexander on 11-07.
conflicts: lint_css_roles.py, assistant.css; CI green at its head, 10-20

dev deleted assistant.css (#2438, dead stylesheets) after this PR edited it: drop that edit, and the file's entry in the lint's list. Alexander left one visible change, the probe stack's focus pill, as Andrew's call.
Keep the incremental cache in the eval worker. The worker's answer carried its whole incremental cache to the page, and the next request carried it back, on every run; now the worker keeps it.
conflicts: Test_WorkerServer.re; CI green at its head, 09-30

test/Test_WorkerServer.re: #2660 (Matt Keenan's, keep incremental evaluation for expensive small programs, merged 11-05) added tests beside these; keep both. Both change the worker's incremental path, so Matt Keenan is the natural reviewer.
Types get a Merkle hash. The evaluator asks is_consistent once per pair of types, not once per copy of them, keyed by a hash kept for each type object.
conflicts: Ascriptions.re; CI green at its head, 10-20
Ascriptions.re, against #2734 (Typ.unroll, Alexander's, merged 11-03). #2681 builds on this PR.

SInt at 32 bits everywhere; overflow an error. use SInt in 2147483647 + 1 was -2147483648 in the browser and 2147483648 natively; now it is an error, everywhere. Small, clean and green, but it changes what programs mean.
merges cleanly; CI green at its head, 11-16
Cyrus: is SInt overflow an error, or a wrap at 32 bits everywhere?
Fewer trampoline bounces. Two small changes to the evaluator's trampoline: half the steps on the PerfBudgets program (206,834 to 96,438), and its budgets lowered to match.
merges cleanly; CI green at its head, 11-03
Matt Keenan, 11-03: 15% faster and 4% less memory, a little less readable, and “ambivalent”. Take it, or close it.

How it goes with issue #2561 (a type mismatch reported on every enclosing form): first, after, or folded in.

Load text about 2.5× faster. The recovering parser (MarkerParse.of_text, for a text FastParse rejects) inserted the text a character at a time, re-grouting each time: now whole tokens, and one re-grout.
merges cleanly; CI green at its head, 09-29
It and #2610 both rewrite that parser's path and conflict with each other in MarkerParse.re; each merges into dev alone. Which first, or one only?
The load fallback through the segmented parser. The same fallback through Parser.to_segment, which splits the text at safe points to avoid the quadratic cost, keeping projectors.

Elaborations without the source's whitespace and comments. Elaborations, sent to the worker with every request, carried each node's whitespace and comments.

A module's sum types usable after it. A sum type declared in a module can be built and matched outside it, not only inside. It came up in Messed Up Dress Up's scripts. #2749 adds tests at its edges, into this branch.
